title: Regional emergency isolator and SLO-driven load-shedding for Dedicated control planes
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and implement an emergency isolator and SLO-driven load-shedding framework for Dedicated/Private control planes to ensure tenant isolation during region outages, upgrades, or capacity pressure. This ticket covers: SLO definitions for tenant-facing control plane endpoints; per-tenant circuit breaker policies with adaptive hysteresis; multi-region failover playbook including progressive traffic siphoning; and automated load-shedding strategies that degrade non-essential work before blocking critical requests.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Define clear control-plane SLOs (API latency P95, error-rate, provisioning throughput) and map remediation actions to SLO breach severity.
  - Implement per-tenant circuit breakers that trip on combined signals (error-rate, kernel queue depth, KV-cache hit drops) and support fast recovery with backoff and operator override.
  - Orchestrate multi-region failover with staged traffic redirection, capacity-aware routing, and tenant-scoped isolation to avoid noisy-neighbor cascade failures.
  - Provide load-shedding tiers (graceful degradation path) that prioritize: control-plane health > production inference traffic > background maintenance tasks.
- Non-goals: application-level model fallback strategies, embedding-cache eviction policies (handled separately).

Design decisions and rationale:
1) SLO ladder and actions:
   - Define three SLO bands for control-plane APIs: GREEN (meets target), YELLOW (degraded, 10-30% breach), RED (severe, >30% breach). For YELLOW we trigger adaptive batching reduction and prefer local cache use. For RED, begin tenant isolation heuristics (see #2).
   - Rationale: early intervention (YELLOW) prevents long-tail escalation and reduces impact on dependent data-plane requests.

2) Tenant-scoped circuit breakers:
   - Each tenant has an independent circuit breaker with inputs: rolling error-rate (5m), average request processing time (1m P95), GPU queue length percent, KV cache hit-rate delta.
   - Policy is hybrid: threshold-based trip + ML-ish scoring that weights correlated signals. Breaker states: CLOSED, SOFT-OPEN (reject background and long-running ops), OPEN (reject non-critical control-plane changes), ISOLATED (network/compute gated until manual or automated recovery).
   - Hysteresis: exponential backoff with jitter and a minimum cool-down of 3 minutes, plus accelerated recovery if downstream metrics normalize.

3) Multi-region failover choreography:
   - Use progressive siphoning: initiate partial diversion to target region for low-risk traffic, measure real-time health and ramp if success. If target region metrics degrade >stop thresholds, abort and fallback to a safety region or degrade workloads.
   - Maintain per-region capacity manifests; routing service consults available capacity and tenant prioritization (critical customers get higher queue weight).
   - Rationale: full instant cutover is too brittle; progressive approach reduces wide-scale cascading.

4) Load-shedding tiers and graceful degradation:
   - Tier 0: Deny maint tasks (backups, cold rebuilds).
   - Tier 1: Deprioritize low-priority Dedicated tenants (based on contract/reservation).
   - Tier 2: Degrade feature set for affected tenants: shorten max sequence length, disable sampling-heavy utilities, return cached/approximate responses.
   - Tier 3: Hard reject non-authenticated or over-quota requests.
   - Each step emits detailed telemetry and a rollback hook to re-enable features as metrics recover.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] SLO documents published in Confluence with thresholds, runbook links, and who-to-call.
- [ ] Per-tenant breaker implemented in control plane with policy API and UI toggle in Console.
- [ ] Multi-region siphon flow tested in staging with canary traffic and automatic rollback on degradation.
- [ ] Load-shedding policy enforced in Dedicated deployment and validated in chaos/load tests.
- [ ] Observability: dashboards for per-tenant breaker state, region capacity, and shed actions; alerting for SLO transitions.

Work plan / milestones:
- Week 1: RFC + SLO definitions; secure review (security and compliance) — (Maya, Arjun).
- Week 2: Prototype per-tenant breaker logic, minimal policy API, unit tests.
- Week 3: Integrate breaker into routing layer; add telemetry. Chaos sim 1: induce kv-cache drop to validate breaker trip.
- Week 4: Implement progressive siphon orchestration; staging failover tests with synthetic traffic.
- Week 5: Load shedding rules and Console controls; PM/Design review of Console UX for isolation controls.
- Week 6: Runbook finalized; cross-team tabletop and production smoke test on canaries; ship feature flags for gradual rollout.

Testing and verification plan:
- Unit tests for breaker state transitions, hysteresis/backoff, and policy evaluation.
- Integration test harness that simulates region-limited capacity and validates siphon/rollback logic.
- K6 load tests for staged load-shedding to ensure latency and error objectives hold for prioritized tenants.
- Chaos experiment: terminate a region's control-plane nodes; verify progressive siphon and that isolation prevents cross-tenant impact.

Security and compliance notes:
- Any isolation that modifies networking or tenant data paths must be reviewed by Security (see release ticket runtime-2.4-security-review).
- Audit logs for isolation decisions and operator overrides are mandatory; include request-level reasons.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should the ML-style scoring be vs. simple thresholds? Aggressive scoring reduces false trips but adds complexity.
- Should the breaker policy be tenant-configurable (per-contract) or centrally managed? Initial plan: centrally managed with operator overrides, then consider per-tenant adjustments for enterprise deals.
- Circuit breaker state persistence: persist across control-plane restarts vs. ephemeral in-memory? Current leaning: persist short-term state (TTL 30m) to avoid thrash during rolling upgrades.

Links and artifacts:
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-17856+-+Regional+Isolator+RFC
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Runbooks+%28Regional+Isolator%29
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/2648
- Staging test dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/dedicated-failover-staging
- Related incident notes: INC-2025-09 (multi-tenant thrash during upgrade), postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-2025-09+Postmortem

Notes on rollout and operator UX:
- Console should show tenant state with a one-click temporary-isolate and reason dropdown. Operator must provide TTL and optional escalation email.
- Feature-flag gate for 2 weeks in staging then progressive tenant opt-in for Dedicated customers.

Next updates will include a link to the initial PR for the breaker implementation and preliminary staging metrics for the chaos run.
